legs.name: São Paulo
legs.blurb: Urban arrival — one night, one long afternoon walk, and the first jolt of Brazil before the wild.

legs.name: Amazon
legs.blurb: Three nights on a clearwater river deep in southern Amazonia — otters at dawn, canopy towers above the treeline, frogs after dark.

legs.name: Pantanal
legs.blurb: The world's largest wetland in the dry season, when the water pulls back and everything comes to the open — jaguar included.

legs.name: Rio de Janeiro
legs.blurb: Back to sea level for the finale — Copacabana, the granite mountains, and the slow wind-down home.

saopaulo.title: The city as canvas
saopaulo.body: A view from the São Paulo Museum of Art. The city's street-art scene exploded after the city banned outdoor billboards in 2006, clearing the way for muralists.

saopaulo.title: Golden arches, translated
saopaulo.body: This São Paulo Mequi - Brazil's nickname for McDonald's - is reportedly the chain's 1,000th location in the country, in a converted early-1900s mansion.

saopaulo.title: Brazilian steak dinner
saopaulo.body: A dinner to remember at Figueira Rubaiyat -- built around a massive fig tree in the dining room -- with picanha, ribeye, palm heart, and pitu shrimp.

amazon.title: The only way in
amazon.body: Landed at Alta Floresta -- from here, the only way to Cristalino Lodge is by truck, then a transfer onto a boat for the final stretch up the river.

amazon.title: Fifteen minutes in
amazon.body: Fifteen minutes into our first boat tour, and we saw a Harpy Eagle -- the most powerful raptor in the Americas

amazon.title: Dwarfed by a tree
amazon.body: Four of us barely wrap around the base of a centuries-old Brazil nut tree, one of the giants of the Cristalino.

amazon.title: Standing their ground
amazon.body: A troop of spider monkeys shook branches and barked warnings, trying to scare us off their patch of canopy.

amazon.title: A wary eye
amazon.body: One of the spider monkey troop pausing mid-branch, keeping a wary eye on us below. Thumbless, they are built to swing by their tails instead.

amazon.title: Through the high canopy
amazon.body: Some of the young spider monkeys had never seen humans before and were more curious than afraid, pausing to watch us as we watched them.

amazon.title: One more frame
amazon.body: Out on the water at sunset, camera up, chasing the day's last good light.

amazon.title: The tree fills up
amazon.body: Neotropical cormorants and cattle egrets crowd a single tree at dusk, stacking up branch by branch.

amazon.title: The sky catches fire
amazon.body: The sky went orange right as the roost tree filled with birds -- one of the best sunsets of the trip.

amazon.title: Riding it in
amazon.body: Heading back to the lodge as the roost tree glowed behind us in the sunset.

amazon.title: Small things, big eyes
amazon.body: A tree frog found on low vegetation during a night walk, clinging to a leaf by its adhesive toe pads.

amazon.alt: A stingless bee, a bromeliad in bloom
amazon.pinLabel: A stingless bee, a bromeliad in bloom
amazon.title: A stingless bee, a bromeliad in bloom
amazon.body: A stingless bee working a pink-coned aechmea in bloom -- one of a thousand tiny scenes at knee height in the Cristalino's understory.

amazon.title: Catching fish
amazon.body: A neotropical otter hauled out on a midstream boulder, grabbing fish with its paws -- we watched it catch seven in a row in the Cristalino river.

amazon.title: The taricaya's tears
amazon.body: Locals call it the taricaya: a yellow-spotted river turtle basking on a rock while butterflies and bees drink its tears, hunting minerals scarce in the Amazon.

amazon.title: Right outside our door
amazon.body: Returning from a hike, we found a capybara grazing a few feet from our room -- close enough to touch.

amazon.title: An unbroken sea of green
amazon.body: Sunrise from the Cristalino Lodge observation deck -- an unbroken carpet of rainforest stretching to the horizon.

amazon.title: The forest exhales
amazon.body: Amazon trees release so much water vapor through transpiration that scientists call the resulting moisture flow a 'flying river'

pantanal.title: The elegant one
pantanal.body: A night encounter with an ocelot, the Pantanal's most elegant small cat -- chain-like rosettes smearing into long streaks.

pantanal.alt: Pampas Deer & Cattle Tyrant — Ozotoceros bezoarticus
pantanal.title: Deer, with bird
pantanal.body: A pampas deer doe crossing open grassland with a passenger -- a cattle tyrant riding her back for flushed insects.

pantanal.title: The Pantanal's emblem
pantanal.body: A Jabiru stork -- the tallest flying bird in the Americas, and widely considered the Pantanal's own emblem -- pulling a fresh crab from the grass with its great upturned bill.

pantanal.title: A cub in daylight
pantanal.body: The headline of the trip: a six-month-old jaguar cub trailing close behind its mother, skittish of us in a way she wasn't.

pantanal.title: Gardener of the forest
pantanal.body: South America's largest land mammal -- known locally as the Brazilian tapir -- out and browsing in the open at midday. Notoriously shy and difficult to track, this was a rare, clear look at one.

pantanal.title: An eight-legged crossing
pantanal.body: A tarantula crossing the track during a safari drive through the Pantanal grounds.

pantanal.title: Early bird gets the snake
pantanal.body: Two southern crested caracaras in a tug-of-war over a snake -- technically part of the falcon family, but nothing like a typical falcon: bold, ground-striding opportunists that scavenge as much as they hunt.

pantanal.title: Ancient and unbothered
pantanal.body: A yacare caiman resting at the water's edge, close enough to count every scale. Hunted hard for its hide in the 1980s, the species has since rebounded to some 10 million strong across the Pantanal.

pantanal.title: Red, white and black
pantanal.body: A yellow-billed cardinal atop a flowering shrub, crisp red, white and black. The name's a bit of a misnomer -- it's actually a tanager, not a true cardinal.

pantanal.title: The largest kingfisher alive
pantanal.body: A ringed kingfisher, the largest kingfisher in the Americas, framed through palm fronds above the water.

pantanal.title: Napping in the open
pantanal.body: The world's largest rodent doesn't hurry for anyone — this one stayed stretched out and dozing in the grass, completely unfazed by our jeep.

pantanal.title: Waiting for a meal
pantanal.body: A trio of lesser yellow-headed vultures waiting on carrion, patient scavengers that quarter low over open country, sniffing out their next meal.

pantanal.title: The largest parrot alive
pantanal.body: A bonded pair of the world's largest flying parrot, cobalt from crown to tail, greeting each other at their nest box.

pantanal.title: Two of a kind
pantanal.body: A bonded pair of the world's largest flying parrot, cobalt from crown to tail.

pantanal.title: An armored shuffle
pantanal.body: A six-banded armadillo shuffling through the evening grass, backlit by the low sun.

pantanal.title: Standing on a fence post
pantanal.body: A burrowing owl -- one that lives underground and hunts by day -- standing tall on a fence post in warm light.

pantanal.title: The continent's largest deer
pantanal.body: A marsh deer buck in full antler -- the continent's largest deer, and one of the Pantanal's Big Five alongside the jaguar, tapir and giant anteater.

pantanal.title: Sneaking closer
pantanal.body: A second jaguar sighting -- this time a pair. The female creeping quietly toward us through the grass, wary but drawing near, the much larger male trailing behind.

pantanal.title: The big male, at rest
pantanal.body: The large male settling into the grass -- a rare, close, calm portrait.

pantanal.title: Following her
pantanal.body: The male trailing after the female, intent on mating.

pantanal.title: Wetland gold
pantanal.body: The Pantanal's wetland lagoon glowing gold at sunset -- a quiet close to a wildlife-packed day.

rio.title: Copacabana Beach
rio.body: Sunset from the rooftop bar at the Emiliano, our hotel on Copacabana, looking out towards the Atlantic Ocean

rio.title: A crash course in Carnaval
rio.body: Carnaval Experience, a working samba-school warehouse in Rio where the floats and sets are built.

rio.title: Front-of-parade fantasia
rio.body: Big opening costume built on a rattan frame so the whole thing rides on one person

rio.title: The wardrobe room
rio.body: Putting on elaborate carnival costumes for fun

rio.title: The Lapa Steps
rio.body: 215 steps that the Chilean artist Jorge Selarón tiled by hand from 1990 until his death in 2013, using tiles sent to him from more than 60 countries.

rio.title: Brothers
rio.body: The green and yellow tiles are Selarón's tribute to Brazil — the country he adopted, and dedicated the staircase to.

rio.title: Corcovado from Dona Marta
rio.body: The mirante looks straight across at the peak: 710 meters of granite with the 30-meter statue standing on top of it.

rio.title: Sugarloaf Mountain
rio.body: The wall at Dona Marta, where the Botafogo Bay opens up, with Sugarloaf Mountain standing out of the water.

rio.title: Through the branches
rio.body: Christ the Redeemer, seen from the Dona Marta lookout

rio.title: Sunset from the halfway stop
rio.body: Morro da Urca is the first of the cable car's two stages -- 220 meters up, with Flamengo, the Aterro, and the Rio-Niterói bridge laid out behind.

rio.title: Morro da Urca stop
rio.body: On Morro da Urca, with Sugarloaf mountain and the cable car behind.

rio.title: The cable line down
rio.body: The cable car run back to Urca strung across an orange sky

rio.title: Everyone waits for the lights
rio.body: Blue hour on Morro da Urca -- Botafogo's curve, the Aterro do Flamengo, and the Serra dos Órgãos far off across Guanabara Bay.

rio.title: Rio, spread out below
rio.body: A sweeping panorama from Corcovado -- beaches, bay, and mountains laid out in one frame.

rio.title: Under open arms
rio.body: Standing right at the base of Christ the Redeemer atop Corcovado, looking straight up at its outstretched arms.
